# Output-Side Normalization: Execution Details

Process receipts, source identities, checksums, controller and keeper
generations, and the automated wave ledger for this endeavor. Split out of
`ENDEAVOR.md` on 2026-11-18 so that the research record reads as a scientific
document; every line here is preserved verbatim from the combined document,
in its original order. Nothing was summarized or deleted.

Read [`ENDEAVOR.md`](ENDEAVOR.md) for the question, method, results and
conclusions. Read this file when you need to verify an artifact, reproduce a
check, or trace which process produced a result.

The 900-second document monitor refreshes the automated ledger section of
this file.

### November 18 Separately Owned Start-Accuracy Trial

Question: does the cancellation-free rational quarter-root start improve
FP32 `O` accuracy on the saved full-shaped CUDA inputs while preserving
the seven unrelated start outputs and eager/capture/replay behavior?
`Ob` and `dn0` are derived from `O` and may change with it.
This is a numerical-start experiment, not a new production training wave.
The isolated root-stage replay does not reproduce the historical
continuous-`f` output; a full-model warm-up/capture-context intervention
remains a separate required experiment.

The new standalone owner comprises `tracking/root_start_gpu_owner.py`,
`root_start_gpu_controller.py`, `root_start_gpu_worker.py` and
`test_root_start_gpu.py`. It calls unchanged accepted
`root_start_execution.run` and preserves every parent helper byte.
Two fresh one-shot processes use opposite pinned/rational variant order
on the complete saved rank-0/update-23 continuous/resumed `B` groups:
`d=(12,512,512)` and `f=(4,2048,2048)`. Each retains all ten outputs for
eager, capture, first replay and second replay. Compilation and explicit
CUDA graphs remain enabled. The FP32 accuracy gate remains
`rtol=1e-5`, `atol=1e-6`; unchanged-output, repeat and cross-process checks
require exact finite equality.

The worker authenticates saved source/configuration/data, physical UUID,
RNG/input layouts and compiled callables under a distinct acknowledged
controller and direct-child marker. Existing node and keeper-manager
locks cover exact keeper transfer and restoration. Worker timeout is
3,600 seconds; canonical evidence paths refuse a rerun. Independent
terminal reconstruction reopens retained outputs and compares FP32 `O`
against the existing independent FP64 log1p/expm1 reference.
The accepted trial's stopping condition is two completed opposite-order
processes, independently reconstructed arithmetic/lifecycle evidence,
original owner/descendant absence and exact eight-device restoration.
Failure remains evidence and never relaxes production gates.

Focused hardened owner tests pass 12/12 in 6.44 seconds, including real
subprocess detached-descendant cleanup, restoration after spawn/nonzero
failure, retained arithmetic and source drift rejection. The complete

accuracy-qualified numerical candidate. It removes
the observed saved-start cancellation error but does not reproduce or
resolve historical root/NS/full-model divergence. The next decisive
experiment must preserve the original full-model warm-up/capture
context and compare the complete root iteration and continuation,
under unchanged tolerance, compilation, graphs and ownership gates.
No start timing was measured, so no efficiency or MuonT-quality claim
follows. Waves 13-15 remain denied until complete candidate validation;
there is no new production history to import to SwanLab.

Separate offline localization plan, November 18 08:53: a read-only source
review identifies a reporting limitation in the frozen continuation
analyzer. `fused_continuation_validation.analysis` passes each rank/update's
whole intermediate-record list to `diagnose_continuation.compare_saved`.
If the continuous/resumed lists have unequal lengths, that comparison
records a sequence-structure difference and returns zero tensor
comparisons for the entire rank/update pair. Unequal refinement/fallback
paths could therefore hide comparable gradients, statistics, factors
and matrix updates. This is a code-level limitation, not an observed
numerical cause of the continuation failure.

the stable stage label within each rank/update pair; repeated matrix
stages also use occurrence within that label's deterministic matrix
traversal. Variable refinement/fallback records remain explicitly unpaired
and retained because the current trace lacks the group/index identity
needed for semantic branch matching. No differing stage labels are paired
by positional coincidence. This reporting successor leaves the current
frozen continuation execution, comparator and receipt unchanged.
Actual saved-intermediate analysis remains denied until the completed
diagnostic records both transparency predicates: trace-off/on losses and
all-rank states at 22/23/24 for both continuous and resumed trajectories,

or a causal intervention.

interventions only and require distinct source-bound candidates:

| Hypothesis | Discriminating Observation or Intervention | CPU Coverage and Remaining Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Process-local graph lifecycle changes the root candidate | Restoration sets `warm=False`: resumed update 23 runs eager and update 24 captures/replays, whereas continuous update 23 can replay its existing graph. After both transparency predicates pass, compare numerical `before_root` inputs and candidate roots. A distinct intervention would synchronize and reset only continuous graph state at boundary 22 while preserving numerical state and RNG. | Bookkeeping can be CPU-tested; eager/capture/replay parity requires CUDA. Expected graph metadata differences alone are not numerical divergence. |
| Pending-refresh restoration changes installed basis/tolerance payloads | Saved pending work is joined and reconstructed as completed futures. Current traces retain pending source steps but omit pre-install host payloads. Compare exact saved payloads and eligible/stale installation decisions; matching pending steps alone cannot prove payload equality. | Round-trip multiple nonidentity owned bases through `engine_state`, `restore_engine` and `install_refreshes`; compare `SB`, `S2`, tolerance, installed/stale decisions and pending removal. This does not establish GPU stream-ordering parity. |
| Repair mutates persistent graph output storage incorrectly | If candidate roots match but finished roots differ, isolate repair from root generation. Separate interventions would copy root/iteration outputs before repair or use independent per-group graph pools, one change at a time. | CPU replay/repair tests can detect alias mutation and wrong-index replacement; CUDA graph-pool lifetime and stream ordering remain GPU-only. |

Restored-root preparation implementation, November 18 11:40-11:49:
`tracking/prepare_restored_roots.py` implements the preparation component
of the root-lifecycle experiment reviewed at 10:11 above. The hypothesis
is that resumed update 23's eager root path and the continuous run's
existing captured-root path may contribute to the observed NS-source
divergence. Preparing kernels on scratch would allow the resumed run to
capture fresh roots on its first actual update; that hypothesis remains
untested on CUDA. The helper is not imported by training, included in
an issued candidate or bound to a GPU controller. The first-resumed-update
fused diagnostic's 97 rank-0 tensor failures at update 23 still have no
demonstrated causal correction.

The helper selects only graph-enabled groups with nonzero ownership,
an installed basis and an optimizer step at or beyond the inline-root
period. Ownership means `group.per > 0`; inline means the initial exact-root
steps before `args.toner_inline`. Readiness is the group's `warm` flag,
which permits `_roots_graphed` to capture instead of taking its first eager
path. It refuses an active update or existing process-local root graph.
For eligible fresh graphs it sets readiness false, orders the side stream
after the current restoration stream, clones only `C`, `tol`, `SB` and
`S2` into independent scratch with exact stride/offset preservation, and
calls the engine's existing `_roots` method outside capture. Scratch roots
are discarded after synchronization. Readiness becomes true only when
all eligible groups and the side stream complete successfully. The helper
does not call `begin`, statistics, pending installation, repair, optimizer
step or NS; it does not publish scratch outputs as training candidates.
Graph-disabled, inline, absent-basis and zero-ownership paths are unchanged.
Kernel compilation/autotuning and CUDA RNG effects remain GPU-unverified.
`C` is the owned covariance EMA, `tol` the acceptance tolerance, and
`SB/S2` the cached basis's two FP16 high/low split layouts. `d/f` identify
the hidden-width and MLP-width input-statistic groups. Only layouts whose
clone retains the original stride and storage offset are accepted.
Contiguous/transposed zero-offset layouts pass; an offset-normalizing
clone raises before readiness is committed.

### Implementation

[`experiment/block_toner.py`](experiment/block_toner.py) implements all
four arms. It contains:

- A BF16 output-row observer for every block projection.
- `OutputToner`, a second Toner fast engine over the output rows.
- `DiagonalMoments` for the diagonal arm.
- `BlockToner`, the per-matrix update of all 224 matrices.

`optimizer.py`, `train.py`, and `capture.py` route the arms; `left_all`
builds the pinned model without input capture. Engine checkpoint state is
in [`experiment/toner_state.py`](experiment/toner_state.py). Configurations
are `experiment/configs/ARM_BATCH_seed0.json` for all four batch families.

The compiled-body row check exposed a weak existing probe.
`synthetic_compiled_body` backpropagates $\operatorname{mean}(h^2)$ of the
final RMSNorm output, which is nearly constant. Its gradients are rounding
noise, and compiled and eager kernels disagree on them by about 180%
relative error even with no observer installed. Its `atol=0.01` hides this.
The new check uses a fixed random readout. With it, compiled and eager
gradients and stored rows agree to about 2%. This does not affect the
wave-0 output collector, which agrees exactly under AOT autograd.

### Pre-Launch Timing Probe

A 200-update execution check of `inner_outer_all` on `28.216.17.9`
(`PVC/validation/smoke_wave1_20261116_0237/`) measured:

| Updates | Median Step Seconds | Rank-0 Output Fallbacks, Cumulative | Max Output Basis Age |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 60-100 | 1.415 | 38 | 5 |
| 150-200 | 1.372 | 82 | 5 |

The wave-0 medians over updates 100-200 are 1.099 s for `muont` and
1.151 s for `outer_left_down`, so `inner_outer_all` was about 25% slower.
Rank-0 peak allocated memory was 24.2 GiB. Output roots needed about 5
repair rounds and 0.4 exact fallbacks per update, against 6 input fallbacks
in 200 updates for wave-0 MuonT. About 20 host refreshes stayed pending.
Output moments drift faster than input moments, and the cached-basis
backend works harder to follow them. `null_all` measures how much of the
slowdown comes from the per-matrix path and output work rather than left
factors. This probe is a timing check, not optimizer evidence.

### Mid-Run Timing, Updates 301-550

Provisional: taken while wave 2 was at roughly update 600 of 5,120. Windows
are matched across waves because output fallbacks accumulate over training,
so an early window understates the output engine. No loss conclusion is
available yet.

| Arm | Output roots | Update path | Median s/update | Versus `muont` | Predicted |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `muont` (wave 0) | none | Toner batched | 1.094 | 0.0% | — |
| `inner_outer_hidden` | dense at 512 only | batched | 1.200 | +9.6% | +6% |
| `inner_outer_leftdiag` | diagonal only | batched | 1.208 | +10.4% | +5% |
| `inner_outer_mlpdiag` | dense at 512, diagonal at 2048 | batched | 1.239 | +13.2% | +7% |
| `outer_left_all` | dense at both widths | batched | 1.306 | +19.3% | +22% |
| `null_all` (wave 1) | dense at both widths | per-matrix | 1.406 | +28.5% | — |
| `inner_outer_all` (wave 1) | dense at both widths | per-matrix | 1.420 | +29.8% | — |

Three corrections to the predictions above.

**Batching helped less than predicted.** `inner_outer_all` on the per-matrix
path minus `outer_left_all` on the batched path is 0.114 s, against a
predicted 0.18-0.20 s, and even that overstates batching alone because
`outer_left_all` also drops the inner left product. The per-matrix
Newton-Schulz loop was therefore not as dominant as wave 1's arm differences
suggested.

**Cheapening the width-2048 output side helped roughly as much as predicted
in absolute terms**, 0.07-0.11 s, but the arms land at +10% rather than +5%
because the batching saving was smaller.

**The residual 10% is not output roots.** `inner_outer_leftdiag` computes no
dense output roots at all and is still 0.114 s above `muont`, and the three
cheap-output arms sit within 0.04 s of each other despite spanning no,
diagonal, and dense width-512 output factors. Dense roots at width 512 are
3.8% of the output eigendecomposition work, so that ordering is consistent.
The residual is therefore in the block path, not the factors.

Arithmetic does not explain it. Output-row capture gathers about
$10^9$ BF16 elements per update across the 224 projections, and the packed
syrk over those rows is roughly 2.8 TFLOP, which are single-digit
milliseconds each on this hardware. Neither accounts for 0.114 s.

#### A Self-Inflicted Share of the Residual

Reviewing `step` against Toner's own found a defect in our code rather than
in the method. The nonfinite guard called `.item()` **inside** the
per-shape-group loop:

```python
for shape, per_rank in self.shape_groups:
    ...
    if not torch.isfinite(delta).all().item():   # host sync, three times per update
        raise FloatingPointError(...)
    works.append((per_rank, *gather_uneven(delta, counts, group=self.pg, async_op=True)))
```

Each `.item()` stalls the host until the whole queued GPU stream drains, and
because it sits before `gather_uneven`, it also stops each group's
all-gather from overlapping the next group's compute. Toner's own `step`
has no such guard. The fix stacks the per-group flags, takes **one** host
wait after every gather is in flight, and still raises before any parameter
changes:

```python
finite.append(torch.isfinite(delta).all())
...                                   # all gathers launched first
checks = torch.stack(finite).tolist()  # one host wait, overlapped with the gathers
```

Two tests cover this, both confirmed to fail when the property they pin is
removed: one checks `step` reproduces the per-matrix equations on CPU, and
one checks that a single nonfinite shape group leaves **every** parameter
unchanged, which is the invariant the batched check has to preserve.

This is a candidate explanation for a large part of the 0.114 s residual,
not a measured one. It also means **the wave-2 timings above carry three
avoidable stalls per update**, since the fix came after launch and the
running processes had already imported the old code. Wave 3's timings should
improve on wave 2's for this reason alone, independently of any change to
the optimizer.

`BlockArm` now carries a separate output side per output width, so an arm
can hold full roots at width 512 and diagonal or no roots at width 2048.
`apply_left_inner` additionally expresses wave 0's outer-only algebra.
Wave 1's arms are unchanged under this generalization, which
[the arm-partition test](experiment/tests/test_block_toner.py) pins.

### Predicted Wave 2 Cost

Recorded before launch, from wave 1's component decomposition and the
width-2048 share of output work. Kept for comparison against the measured
window above, which shows the batching term was overestimated.

| Arm | Output work removed | Predicted s/update | Versus `muont` |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `inner_outer_all` with batching | none | $\approx$ 1.34 | +22% |
| `outer_left_all` | none; algebra only | $\approx$ 1.34 | +22% |
| `inner_outer_mlpdiag` | 96% of eigh, 86% of Gram | $\approx$ 1.17 | +7% |
| `inner_outer_hidden` | same, and the rows too | $\approx$ 1.16 | +6% |
| `inner_outer_leftdiag` | all dense output work | $\approx$ 1.15 | +5% |

Two assumptions carry these numbers: that batching recovers the 0.18-0.20 s
update-path cost, and that the output engine's 0.19 s scales with the
$d^3$ share. Both are untested. The first is bounded by the fact that
`muont` already runs a batched path at 1.095 s, so 1.34 s would still leave
the block path 0.19 s above a batched arm carrying a dense input engine.

The question wave 2 answers is whether `inner_outer_all`'s -0.0061
selection-loss gain survives cheapening the width-2048 output side. If
`inner_outer_mlpdiag` keeps most of it at +7% step time, that is a better
optimizer than `muont` at near-parity cost. If the gain disappears, the
width-2048 output rotation was carrying it, and the honest conclusion is
that the gain costs 22% and is not worth it at this scale.

`BlockArm` carries a separate output side per output width, so an arm can
hold full roots at width 512 and diagonal or no roots at width 2048.
`apply_left_inner` expresses wave 0's outer-only algebra and `lag_left` the
deferred-application variant. Wave 1's arms are unchanged under these
generalizations, which [the arm-partition test](experiment/tests/test_block_toner.py)
pins.

### Early Loss Read, Updates 513-1024

Provisional and directional only: wave 2 was near update 1,200 of 5,120.
Paired train-loss window means against wave-0 `muont`, negative being
better. Early windows overstate: `inner_outer_all`'s own advantage shrank
from -0.00890 at this window to -0.00519 by the end, a factor of 1.7.
Held-out selection loss, which is what arms are chosen on, is not yet
available.

| Arm | Δ train, 513-1024 | Share of `inner_outer_all` | Step time vs `muont` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `inner_outer_all` (wave 1) | -0.00890 | 100% | +29.8% |
| `inner_outer_mlpdiag` | -0.00674 | 76% | +13.2% |
| `inner_outer_leftdiag` | -0.00595 | 67% | +10.4% |
| `inner_outer_hidden` | -0.00107 | 12% | +9.6% |
| `null_all` (wave 1 control) | +0.00135 | — | +28.5% |

Two findings are already separable, and both bear directly on the
efficiency question.

**Width-2048 output geometry carries most of the gain, but only its
diagonal is needed.** `inner_outer_hidden`, which drops the MLP-width
output factors entirely, keeps almost none of the advantage and sits near
the null control. `inner_outer_mlpdiag`, which keeps those rows but
replaces their dense roots with elementwise powers, keeps roughly
three-quarters of it. So the information in the width-2048 output moment is
largely in its scale, not its rotation, and that is the cheap part: the
dense roots it removes are 96.2% of the output eigendecomposition work.

**Wave 1's verdict on the diagonal was confounded, as suspected.**
`inner_outer_all_diag` was worse than `muont` and the stated caveat was
that it diagonalized the input side too. `inner_outer_leftdiag` diagonalizes
only the output side and keeps two-thirds of the gain at +10.4% step time.
The diagonal output approximation is therefore sound; wave 1's result was
about the input side.

If these hold to 5,120 updates with the same 1.7 shrinkage, `mlpdiag` lands
near -0.004 at +13.2%, against `inner_outer_all`'s -0.005 at +29.8%. That
would be the first arm in this endeavor to beat `muont` at close to parity
cost. It is a projection from two windows, not a result.

### CPU Checkpoint Diagnosis and Follow-Up

The read-only CPU diagnostic completes at 21:55:14 after 112.8 seconds:
`python tracking/diagnose_continuation.py --root PVC --out PVC/run-preparation/diagnostic-wave6-muont-continuation-20261116.json`.
It checks every preserved reference rank at both update 22 and update 24,
hashes all 32 checkpoint files, and binds conclusions to the frozen source,
helpers, archive and original failure receipts. Diagnostic SHA256:
`7e86199319cb764d357703797d8021a15957ebf260b5147c29454c5edb71b37e`.

| Boundary | Compared Tensors | Changed / Failing Tensors | Scalar or Structure Differences |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 22 | 2221 | 0 / 0 | 0 |
| 24 | 2195 | 18 / 18 | 8 |

All saved input EMA tensors remain bitwise exact at update 24. Only the
down-input factor groups on ranks 0, 1 and 3 differ: saved bases,
tolerances, pending-refresh ages and, on rank 3, fallback/repair counters.
No changed momentum, auxiliary optimizer or RNG tensor is reported.
The three model-weight failures are:

| Down Matrix | Maximum Error | Entries Outside Original Tolerance |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Block 3 | 0.000160091 | 976618 / 1048576 |
| Block 7 | 0.000158526 | 977216 / 1048576 |
| Block 12 | 0.000237256 | 990088 / 1048576 |

This supports investigating post-resume cached-root execution and
wall-time-dependent host-refresh installation, not blaming output reduction
or the shared data stream. It does not yet identify a causal root bug.
Raw saved basis differences can include eigenvector sign choices, so their
large entrywise errors alone are not evidence of a similarly large root
error. The parameter divergence and changed refresh ages are the decisive
failure evidence.

The next proposed experiment is a separately bound **fixed-age refresh
scheduling control**: retain reference precision, NS, model, factors and
CUDA graphs, but make pending-basis installation depend on a fixed update
age rather than `Future.done()` timing. At each deterministic installation
point, join eligible refreshes on both continuous and resumed paths and
record the source/installation update. Restore the same pending ages and
require exact update-22 plus original-tolerance update-24 continuation.
Compare a same-source MuonT scheduling control before attributing loss or
throughput effects to outer-only geometry. The extra host wait is a
measurable systems cost, not an assumed efficiency gain. This follow-up is
proposed, not implemented, GPU-validated, queued or launched; the failed
frozen wave-6 candidate is retained unchanged.

## Verification and Remaining Work

This audit confirmed complete manifests, 5,120 consecutive unique JSONL
updates per arm, matching token counts, unchanged bound source/config/data
identities, final checkpoint receipts, and stopped training processes.
Earlier launch evidence includes 18 passing CPU tests, synthetic A100/NCCL
checks, collector/packing/FA2/down-update checks, and exact zero-error
full-model continuous-three versus two-plus-resume comparisons for all arms.

Those checks do not establish full-budget H100/FA3 parity, complete
microbatch-8 versus microbatch-4 model trajectories, or an optimizer-equivalent
zero-output-factor control using the custom down path.
During the original audit, full-model checkpoint continuation after the
cached-root transition remained unverified and only synthetic post-transition
inputs were tested. The Wave-7 fixed-age control subsequently passes actual
all-rank continuous24 versus22+resume24 on all four arms at 22:49:38,
without changing tolerances. That evidence applies to its new scheduling
policy; the earlier dynamic-installation candidates retain their failures.

Recommended order before claiming an output-side benefit:

1. Build a custom-down **null-output control**: output strength zero/identity,
   with the same per-matrix NS, root-product arithmetic, collection work,
   checkpoints, and scheduling as outer-left. Compare its actual down updates
   with upstream MuonT to bound execution differences.
2. On a short matched-data run, compare gradients, pooled input moments,
   roots, and updates between microbatch 8 and 4. A synthetic single-linear
   partition test is not full-model equivalence. Keep global batch fixed.
3. If exact runtime reproduction is required, use the pinned H100/FA3
   environment and upstream microbatch 8. Otherwise explicitly retain the
   A100-adapted claim and use within-runtime controls.
4. Follow the fair LR/output-strength tuning below using held-out
   mixture selection loss. Keep C4 as reporting data; avoid repeatedly
   selecting hyperparameters from its 236 windows.
5. Confirm selected candidates with paired seeds, matching initial weights,
   sample streams, token budgets, runtime, and checkpoint cadence. Report
   seed-wise deltas and uncertainty; adjacent evaluations of one seed are
   not independent replications.
6. Test 1M/2M/4M batches using their own upstream LR/schedule settings if
   batch sensitivity is the next question. Do not reuse the 0.5M schedule
   unchanged or equate a larger reference gap with a guaranteed new-arm gain.

#### Upstream-Product and Null Follow-Up, November 17

**Question.** Does diagonal output scaling retain its fixed-token gains
while using the pinned MuonT input and combined outer-product kernels?
The existing custom block path uses eager FP32 dense products; pinned
MuonT uses `roots.rows_lo`, compiled `engine.muont_in`, batched NS,
and compiled `engine.muont_out`. Execution differences confound runtime
and small numerical loss differences. Reusing the pinned products is
an unmeasured efficiency hypothesis.

The isolated candidate is
`PVC/candidates/upstream-outer-fixed-age-0p5m-20261117/`.
It copies the frozen Wave-8 candidate and its materialized pinned
Toner revision `dab7f3777c75e740536df822f50ffa1d929a340c`.
Only the new module, arm dispatch, scalar buffer, two 0.5M configs,
cluster list, fail-closed execution owner and candidate-specific tests
change. Original Wave-8 source, configuration, validation and release
bindings remain unchanged.

For an $m\times n$ weight matrix, let $R_{\rm in},R_{\rm out}$ be the
existing dense input factors and $l_{\rm out}$ the collected diagonal
output factor. Define
$\widehat R=R_{\rm out}\sqrt n/\|R_{\rm out}\|_F$,
$\widehat L=\operatorname{diag}(l_{\rm out}/
\sqrt{\operatorname{mean}(l_{\rm out}^2)})$ and
$s=\sqrt{\max(1,m/n)}$. The intended equation is

$$
M_t=\mu M_{t-1}+G_t,\qquad
Q_t=\operatorname{NS}((G_t+\mu M_t)R_{\rm in}),
$$

$$
\Delta W=-\eta\left(s\widehat LQ_t\widehat R+
\lambda W\widehat R^2\right).
$$

The implemented candidate calls pinned `muont_in` and NS unchanged,
multiplies the NS output by the RMS-normalized left diagonal, then
calls pinned `muont_out`. The input-side weight-decay equation is
unchanged. A device scalar buffer supplies scheduled LR and decay;
its host-to-device transfer cost is unmeasured. The production
configuration retains `ns_mode="tpu"` and all existing compile/graph
settings; CPU references do not emulate those CUDA kernels.

| New Arm | Output Collection | Output Application | Input / NS / Outer Products |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `outer_leftdiag_upstream_fused` | Existing fused diagonal collector | Outer scaling only | Pinned MuonT products |
| `null_leftdiag_upstream_fused` | Same collector and output statistics | Disabled, $\widehat L=I$ | Pinned MuonT products |

The null controls output application while retaining collection cost.
Whole-model numerical equivalence to MuonT remains unverified.
Only 0.5M configs exist for these arms. They retain seed 0, eight ranks,
microbatch 4, 5,120 updates, 2,684,354,560 tokens, LR 0.02262741696,
weight decay 0.1, momentum 0.95, ten NS steps and refresh-install age 1.
No 1M/2M/4M settings were invented.

Direct FP64 products check the output equation, input decay and zero
LR over square/tall/wide shapes. FP32 direct-product controls check

Nesterov settings. Step tests check resulting parameters and retained

### Owned Outer-Factor Follow-Up, November 17

**Hypothesis.** The original upstream outer/null path constructs diagonal
inner and outer factors for all224 output projections on every rank,
although each rank updates only28 projections. Outer-only arms never
use the inner output roots. Restrict factor construction to locally used
outer vectors while retaining all existing observed moments and state.
This should reduce factor arithmetic and Python object construction;
the amount of whole-training saving remains unmeasured. It does not
remove the output-row collection or communication overhead.

`tracking/prepare_owned_output.py` starts from the exact issued Wave-9
source and creates a distinct candidate. `OwnedOutputMoments` inherits
the original `DiagonalMoments` collection, pooled EMA/reduction and
checkpoint schema. Pinned `toner.fast.engine.layer_counts` supplies the
contiguous eight-rank ownership partition. Factor normalization,
damping, exponent and zero-trace behavior retain their original equations,
operating only on the owned contiguous slices. Each factor is
`(None, outer)`. No unowned moment or cotangent buffer is dropped.
Only `outer_leftdiag_upstream_fused` and its matched null use this path;
legacy and MuonT remain unchanged. The null still constructs the same
owned outer vectors as the active output arm.

passes137 CPU tests at12:04:01 but generated-source formatting
needs correction. It remains preserved. Distinct numerical successor

at12:08:15; its changed generated sources pass repository Ruff/Black.

The candidate is the preserved training source/configuration directory
`PVC/candidates/selected-lr-wave12-post-failure-formatted-20261117`.
The controller is the helper bundle that verifies, publishes and runs
that candidate. The session-tested generation contains 51 helper files,
including the archived keeper manager. Both its exact file inventory
and all 34 original numerical-validation helpers match the controller
receipt and unchanged original validation binding.

The keeper manager and recovery worker now share one node-local exclusive
file lock. A keeper is the background matrix-multiplication workload
that occupies GPUs between experiments. The worker holds this reservation
through allocation release,
training, cleanup and keeper restoration. Restoration passes the same
open descriptor to the local manager, continuing ownership of the same
locked file description without acquiring a different descriptor.
The manager checks the lock's file identity; its long-lived keeper child
closes the descriptor before launch. The worker releases the reservation
after restoration and final state publication. Independent manager
actions return 75 while the reservation is held.
The keeper pointer is the file containing the manager's current launcher
PID. An accepted generation is the exact launcher/eight-rank set whose
PID, kernel start ticks, ancestry, session, command and GPU occupancy
match the recorded post-failure restoration. Holding the shared lock
prevents a cooperating manager from publishing a replacement while the
recovery helper terminates that set and removes its pointer.

Before deployment, read-only review finds no remaining blocker in the
wiring and requires deployed source verification and actual child
descriptor closure. The later all-node deployment and CPU launch tests
below satisfy those two review requirements.
Both standalone and inherited-lock CPU-only manager launches verify
that the published keeper PID equals its process-group and session IDs,
no manager-lock descriptor or inherited lock variable remains in the
child, and the lock becomes available while that child remains live.

10 tests in 0.94 seconds. Scoped Ruff, Black, license, syntax and whitespace
checks pass; canonical manager Bash syntax also passes. These checks use

Preparation moved from the initial worker count to 96 workers and local
scratch with block copies to avoid small-write waits on the PVC FUSE mount.
The upstream tokenizer/preparer was unchanged. The wrapper loaded only
`HF_TOKEN`, held an output lock, verified the full plan, and issued the
training/C4 receipt only after verification.

Validation failures constrain the reproduction claim:

- Optional TCCL Inspector initialization caused SIGILL; runs set
  `NCCL_INSPECTOR_ENABLE=0` while retaining NCCL and root CUDA graphs.
- Microbatch 8 exhausted A100 memory during head autotuning; every active
  configuration moved to microbatch 4 with unchanged global batch/budget.
- Candidate split-product/batched BF16 down updates exceeded existing
  parity tolerance; the retained path uses direct FP32 root products and
  per-matrix upstream NS.
- Unrestricted compiler autotuning and DDP bucket changes failed fresh
  versus resumed comparisons. ATEN-only body/head GEMMs, precision-cast
  emulation, deterministic algorithms, and fixed initial DDP buckets
  preceded the passing comparisons. No tolerance was relaxed.
- Output observation buffers required independent per-layer storage to
  avoid compiled-backward saved-buffer version conflicts.

Final real-data continuous-three versus two-plus-resume checks compared
3707/2003/2027/1995 tensors for Muon/MuonT/outer-left/hybrid across eight
ranks with zero maximum absolute error. Synthetic cached-root continuation
saved after update 22 and continued through update 24; it controlled host
refresh readiness. Full-model asynchronous post-transition continuation
was unverified by these original Wave-0 gates. The distinct Wave-7
fixed-age candidate subsequently passes four-arm full-model
continuous24 versus22+resume24 at 22:49:38; this does not retroactively
approve the earlier dynamic-installation candidates.

History receipts under `PVC` include `run-preparation/access.json`,
`source-file-access.json`, `first-shards.json`, `preparation-state.json`,
`full-loader.json`, `preflight-data-ready.json`,
`keeper-release-20261115.json`, `validation-gpu.json`, `wave0.json`,
and `wave0-live.json`. Preparation and GPU-check logs retain the failed
attempts. The initial data-access failure log is
`PVC/run-preparation/prepare-data-attempt-20261115.log`; completed preparation
is logged in `PVC/run-preparation/prepare-full-scratch-20261115.log`.
GPU checks used `PVC/validation/attempt_20261115_1348/gpu_checks.json`,

`attempt_20261115_1407/gpu_checks.json`, and the final
`PVC/validation/attempt_20261115_1418/` directory.

All completed full-budget waves (0-4, 7-10, 12) are imported and verified.
Waves 5/6 stopped at validation and have no full-budget training histories.
Wave 11 failed before its first optimizer update; Wave 12 is its separately
identified recovery, not an independent scientific replication.
The wave-1 receipt is
`PVC/run-preparation/swanlab-upload-wave1.json`; wave 0's is the
`-wave0` file. `swanlab_upload.py --wave WAVE` selects the wave, and
re-invocation verifies rather than duplicating cloud runs. Wave 3's original
upload log records all four verified by 17:03:57 on November 16; read-only
reverification refreshed all four receipts by 17:50:36. Wave 4 completed
at 19:40:41; `swanlab-upload-wave4.json` records all four full-resolution
histories verified at 19:43:47.

Compare unsmoothed validation loss at matched tokens and plot candidate
minus input-MuonT deltas. Loss is `train/loss`, C4 is `eval/c4_loss`, and
selection is `eval/selection_loss`. Runtime scalars are under `runtime/`.
Sparse evaluations are not filled or interpolated.

Cloud verification checked every scalar column at full resolution.
Steps and integer metrics match exactly; CSV-export floats differ by at
most two float64 ULPs, recorded per column in the upload receipt.
This serialization tolerance does not apply to training tests.
Cloud duration and wall-clock axes describe import time.

The [logging runbook](tracking/README.md) documents repeatable import,
read-only verification, and offline tests. It uses isolated
`swanlab==0.10.5` and `python-dotenv==1.2.4`, loads only `SWANLAB_API_KEY`,
and disables uploader hardware/environment/git monitoring and terminal
capture. No credentials, datasets, checkpoints, or source archives were
uploaded.
